headline: Sweden Caretaker Government Sends 2027 Budget Bill to Parliament
deck: The proposal retains planned defence investment and seeks more transport funding, but its submission does not enact spending.
body: Sweden’s caretaker government submitted its 2027 budget bill to the Riksdag on Thursday, the Finance Ministry said. Reuters reported that the measure promises continued defence investment and more transport funding while refraining from major new policy initiatives. The official confirmation establishes the bill’s delivery to Parliament; it does not enact the proposed spending. [E1] [E8]

Government-formation talks remained under way after September’s election, Reuters reported, leaving the bill largely a holding budget without significant reforms. Reuters also reported that the budget maintained forecasts of 3.0% economic growth for 2026 and 2.3% for 2027, alongside core-inflation outlooks of 1.5% and 2.3%. [E2] [E3]

The government said previously planned investments to reinforce Sweden’s total defence would remain, with adjustments, because total defence must continue to function in a turbulent international environment. It also proposed higher transport-infrastructure funding based on defence needs. This paper’s 30 October coverage described Andreas Norlén’s proposed government of the Centre Party, Social Democrats, Christian Democrats, Green Party and Liberals. [E4] [E5] [E9]

The government said unchanged appropriations could slow defence reinforcement and disrupt necessary activities. It also said the defence financing has support from all parties in the Riksdag. [E6] [E7]

evidence_box.fragment: Sweden's right-wing caretaker government on Thursday presented a budget bill for 2027, promising to continue a buildup in defence and more investment in transport infrastructure, but refraining from major new policy initiatives.
